system.description:
In Dark Medieval Europe, it is not very difficult to simply assume another name and identity, provided one knows everything necessary to pass as the assumed persona. Especially in Cainite circles, where records of lineage and age-old allegiances make backgrounds easier to verify, a well-established identity takes years — often decades — to create and build. This Background represents that time and effort, and thus how difficult it is for others to find inconsistencies in a Charlatan's false persona (and how much status that persona can confer). The actual ability to act as a member of another clan falls under Subterfuge; this Background merely represents how well the cover story itself holds up to scrutiny. Players can take this Background multiple times at multiple levels for multiple identities; Storytellers are free to limit its use and demand detailed explanations, and false identities often require the help of allies to establish.

System: Storytellers can use 5 + Alternate Identity as the difficulty on extended investigative actions undertaken to find the truth behind the cover identity. At one dot the identity holds up to casual interaction but folds under real scrutiny; at five dots the identity is impeccable, known and respected across several fiefs, and even elders will vouch for the character should the truth threaten to come to light.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis IV: Thieves in the Night, Book One: Charlatans
